facts.raw_span: A young girl initially came under care at age 4 years
developed an irregular brown-black patch on her left lateral ankle, measuring 3.6 × 3 cm
triangular hyperpigmented, asymptomatic patch consisting of confluent mottled black and brown macules and several satellite lesions
slow but progressive growth of the hyperpigmented patch, which had increased to 5.5 × 5-cm
two discrete areas of regression were noted
discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas with gray-brown structureless areas and a negative pigment network were observed
No induration was palpated except at the previous biopsy site
Shows a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction consistent with an atypical compound nevus
Shows atypical nevus with areas of dermal fibrosis
Score: -7.1 (where scores from -16.7 to -2.1 are consistent with a benign nevus)
A large, dark brown patch consisting of coalescing macules and satellite lesions
Compound melanocytic proliferation with appropriate maturation, random atypia with large nested cells characterized by prominent nucleoli and heavy pigmentation

concepts.why: The presence of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, along with atypical nevus features and dermal fibrosis, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's age at onset and the characteristics of the hyperpigmented patch are consistent with a congenital melanocytic nevus.
The patient's family history and the presence of atypical melanocytic lesions with regression support this diagnosis.
Although the gene expression testing score is consistent with a benign nevus, the presence of atypical features and dermal fibrosis cannot rule out melanoma entirely.
The patient's congenital melanocytic nevus and the presence of satellite lesions support this diagnosis, although no clear evidence of neurological involvement is present.
The presence of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, along with atypical nevus features, could also be consistent with a Spitz nevus.
The patient's hyperpigmented patch with blue-gray areas and a negative pigment network could be consistent with a blue nevus.
The patient's congenital melanocytic nevus and the presence of satellite lesions could be consistent with a nevus of Ito or Ota, although the location is not typical.
